text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.allowM: A different question from Compatibility risk: that one is whose code, this one is whose mob.
Off: a mob whose class comes from a mod never paths off-thread. Measured as zero, not merely fewer.
On: those mobs are treated like vanilla ones, running navigation code nobody has inspected.
Unsafe already includes this. It waives one check, not all of them; Audited keeps the rest.
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.compat: Which mods may have modified pathfinding while PathWeaver still runs searches off-thread.
About other mods' code, not about which mobs qualify. If your pack is refused, nothing runs off-thread.
Audited: trusts bytecode audits and a bounded call-sample. Lean packs pass; heavy packs run nothing.
Unsafe (default): no checks, runs uninspected mod code on workers. Back up your world.
The startup log says which one your pack landed on, and /pathweaver status repeats it. Restart to apply.
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.enable: Master switch. Off returns pathfinding to vanilla at once: no new off-thread searches, no repath reuse.
Searches already accepted finish normally. Safe to toggle at any time.
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.maxInF: Maximum searches queued or running at once
An admission limit, not a buffer. Raising it does not help.
A deeper queue makes each result land later, and one arriving after its mob asked again is discarded.
On a 371-mod pack, 1024 left 91% of dispatched searches uninstalled in the capture window; 4096, nearly all.
Lowering wastes less but pushes searches onto the main thread. 256 measured best. Restart to apply.
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.maxRes: Leave at default. How long a finished search stays usable after it completes.
Measured at 10 and 200 ticks with no difference outside noise.
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.repath: Reuse a valid path if the target moved less than (blocks)
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.brainS: Villagers, piglins, frogs and allays ask for paths in a way the other settings never see.
On, their searches move to a worker thread, at the cost of one tick before the mob sets off.
On the reference pack this was the largest block of pathfinding that could be moved off it.
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.stalen: Discard results after the mob moves (blocks)
Do not set this near zero. A finished search is discarded if its mob moved farther than this.
A moving mob always moves: at 0, 91.8% of dispatched searches were never installed in the window.
The mod then does essentially nothing while appearing to work. 4 is the default and is fine.
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.truste: Mod ids to run on worker threads without auditing them, leaving the scan armed for everything else.
The scoped version of Unsafe: accept the mods you have decided about, not every mod you ever install.
Not a safety feature. These run unchecked, exactly as Unsafe would, just aimed at fewer mods.
Matched by mod id, so an entry keeps applying after that mod updates. Restart to apply.
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.worker: Switch a mob family off after N failures
If a search crashes on a worker this many times, that mob family paths normally again for the rest of the session.
A safety net, not a fix: it catches crashes, not a bad path produced without one.
Set to 0 to never switch anything off; failures are still logged and counted.
A session total also trips it: whichever is higher, this setting or 25. At 0, nothing trips.
Failures only count while close together. 1200 ticks is about a minute on a healthy server, longer on a struggling one.
The idea: a real incompatibility fails in a burst, an isolated hiccup does not. 0 = never forget a failure.
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.title: PathWeaver
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.poolTh: 0 picks one thread per 4 CPU threads: 4 on a 16-thread box, 8 on a 32-thread one.
Raising it is almost never the fix. Profiled on a 32-thread machine, the pool sat 99% idle.
Searches are limited by the in-flight cap, not by thread count.
Raise it only if status shows requests waiting for a free worker. Restart to apply.
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.repath: Reuses the current path when the target moved less than this many blocks. 0 turns reuse off.
Default 1. This avoids searches outright rather than moving them to a worker.
Raise it if mobs re-target constantly; lower it if they walk to slightly stale destinations.
text.autoconfig.pathweaver.option.result: Lets one mob reuse a route another already computed, when every input to the search is identical.
A route is dropped the moment a block changes along it, so a reused route is never a stale one.
Shadow (default) counts the hits without spending them, so you can see what Serve would be worth.
/pathweaver status prints the count. Switching modes takes effect at once, no restart.
How long a route stays offerable. Default 40, which is two seconds.
Not the safety limit: a block change along the route drops it whatever this says.
It bounds drift the cache cannot see, such as a door another mob has opened since.
How many routes to hold before the least recently used one is dropped. Default 4096.
Each entry is one route plus its list of world sections. Raise it on worlds with many mobs.
